findings.reason: the measurement node would pool the pre-fix runs, where the arm measured "no edit tool", into the treatment arm, so an adoption verdict could read "do not adopt" from an attenuated treatment rather than from the tool.
findings.text: §10 records that the one run carrying the anchored treatment recorded `anchored_edit: true` and never had the tools, while §8 (line 106) splits its treatment population on exactly that field and the new §8→§10 dependency only orders the dispatch: nothing bounds the window, discards the runs already recorded `true`, or adds a fact that separates a treated-launch run from a broken-launch run

findings.reason: the population query the section's verdict rests on has nothing to split on in the store, so either §4 must land the field in the store or §8 must name the run directory or ledger as its read source.
findings.text: §8 divides the arms on the run record's `anchored_edit` field and says every metric is "read from the run store, never from prose", but that field is in no run-store row: 0 of 11,265 `run_details` rows in `run_store.db` carry it (nor `fenced`, its sibling), the cited run's own `runs` row has a null `payload`, and the value exists only in the run directory's `worker.json`

findings.reason: the plan offers "make the server start faster" as its second candidate remedy, asks the node to measure which works, and its live check would catch a wrong choice, so the unproven first candidate costs a round rather than a wrong landing.
findings.text: §10 attributes the absent tools to the server's 5.5–6.3 s start, but its cited session-start record has every MCP server except `imas-dd` in `pending` (including the long-established `reckon` server), no later record reports whether `reckon-anchored-edit` ever connected, and the run's one `ToolSearch` result reports `total_deferred_tools: 39`, so deferral cannot be excluded as the mechanism

findings.reason: a node can close on an environment variable that changes nothing and the cost is paid in a coordinator-run dispatch; requiring a recorded local launch whose session-start record reaches `connected` before the remedy is chosen removes that failure mode.
findings.text: §10's done-when accepts a test showing the launch environment "carries the startup allowance" as its node-local measure, while the deliverable itself says "whichever the node measures to work": nothing requires the node to record that the allowance made the server connect before the first turn, so the only measure that the tools are actually offered is the coordinator's live run, dispatched after the node lands
